objective: Test whether one repository CAS lineage record keyed by a stable logical resource key can replace provider reverse-history reconstruction while fencing stale/current-incarnation confusion, ambiguous retry, takeover, and quota-zero/rate-limit interruption.

candidate_protocol: Read the current repository record and require a current-blob CAS for every lineage transition.
Before any authoritative effect, compare the effect target's currently observed opaque provider ID with current_provider_id; mismatch fails closed until a lineage CAS installs the new incarnation.
Use applied_transition_id as a durable read-before-retry identity after an ambiguous CAS response or coordinator takeover.
Never require a reverse predecessor lookup for normal reconciliation once predecessor_id_digest_or_tombstone is present.
On repository read/rate-limit interruption, perform no authoritative effect and checkpoint for a later invocation.

public_source_observations.source: GitHub Docs: Using global node IDs
public_source_observations.observation: GitHub documents REST node_id / GraphQL id as an opaque object reference usable for direct node lookup and recommends persisting global node IDs for integrations.

GitHub documents repository transfer and optional rename, including cases where an OWNER/REPOSITORY-NAME combination can be permanently retired. The checked page does not state a monotonic lineage epoch or anti-rollback witness for integrations.

model.weighting: Equal-weight finite mechanism lattice; counts are counterexample/mechanism counts, not production probabilities.
model.scope_note: rename/transfer_same_provider_object is an adversarial same-provider-ID ABA control, not a claim that GitHub documentation guarantees node-ID preservation on every transfer. The model asks whether provider-ID equality alone can detect a repository epoch rollback if the same object remains the effect target.

reverse_history_baseline.interpretation: Reverse-history dependence fails the Part94 lost-predecessor objective and still does not solve same-provider-ID witness rollback.

cas_record_only_no_current_target_check.interpretation: A CAS lineage file by itself is not authority when the provider incarnation can change outside that CAS domain.

cas_plus_current_provider_id_plus_applie.interpretation: The repository lineage witness removes reverse-history dependence for the tested non-rollback cases and safely detects new-provider-ID reuse via current-target comparison. applied_transition_id resolves ambiguous retry/takeover only while the witness itself has not been rewound.

hypothetical_external_monotonic_epoch_po.reason: It assumes an anti-rollback epoch outside the repository rollback domain, which is exactly the residual coordination capability under test and cannot be imported as a zero-dependency solution.

finding.positive_narrow_scope: Within the tested scope where the repository lineage record is not force-rewound, CAS + current-target provider-ID comparison + applied_transition_id had 0 unsafe stale effects and 0 duplicate authoritative effects across 48 transport-available scenarios; eight current-provider mismatches failed closed. It also does not require predecessor reverse lookup for those reconciliations.
finding.falsification: Under force-rewind/restore of the same repository authority domain, a same-provider-object rename/transfer ABA can restore an older incarnation_epoch/applied_transition_id while current provider-ID equality still passes. All 16 such transport-available scenarios were stale-authority counterexamples; the four ambiguous-response+takeover combinations duplicated an authoritative effect.
finding.minimal_unresolved_child: A zero-cost, zero-finite-quota anti-ABA/fencing mechanism for same-provider-ID lineage transitions whose monotonic evidence survives repository authority force-rewind/restore without richer-mode, protected-primary, manual-user execution, or an external hosted coordinator. Alternatively, prove a narrower effect class has sink-native durable idempotency/current-state preconditions strong enough that witness rollback cannot cause a duplicate or stale authoritative effect.

zero_dependency_zero_quota_assessment.repository_transport_role: Lightweight state/evidence transport only; rate-limit/read interruption is fail-closed and not treated as compute.

scope_guard: This result is limited to the stated 192-scenario abstract identity/effect model and the two cited public GitHub documentation pages. It does not claim a production failure rate, does not claim undocumented node-ID behavior on transfer, and does not prove safety against repository rollback beyond the modeled controls.
continuation: Part96: execute exactly one bounded anti-ABA substitute leaf for the same-provider-ID rollback counterexample. Compare (A) repository witness only, (B) target/sink current-state CAS precondition keyed by stable applied_transition_id, and (C) hypothetical independent monotonic floor as a non-accepted positive control. Use one small finite lattice covering witness force-rewind, sink state advance then rollback/no-rollback, ambiguous effect response, takeover/retry, same-provider rename/transfer ABA, repository rate-limit interruption, and sink idempotency retention loss. Accept a repository/target-native route only if stale authority and duplicate authoritative effects remain zero without any richer-mode/protected/manual step, finite monthly/trial/paid quota, external hosted coordinator, or incremental monetary cost; otherwise preserve the exact sink-atomicity/anti-rollback residual child and choose a distinct next authority leaf for the following invocation.
